why: MI-280 unit U14. Closes BL-20260912-MERGE-SLOT-STATE-DEFAULTED-AN-UNANSWERABLE-PR-PAYLOAD-TO-OPEN-AND-GRADED-IT-LIVE, filed and fixed in the same change. Tier-1 tooling: scripts/ops/**, tests/**, docs/claude/health-review-backlog.json. No src/, no config/, no deploy/, no order path. NOT landing machinery — scripts/ops/merge_slot_state.py is absent from check_pr_landing.py::LANDING_MACHINERY, checked by importing the module and reading all twelve entries (claim_merge_slot.py IS one; merge_slot_state.py is not); the only entry this diff matches is the `.github/pr-landing/*.json` glob, i.e. this declaration, which R12 excludes by construction. FOUND IN USE, not by reading the code, and in the module this same session wrote three units earlier to refuse exactly this shape: settling a merge-slot incumbent, the board `purpose` carried no `#NNNN`, so the PR number came out EMPTY, `GET /repos/.../pulls/` returned `{'message': 'Request path could not be canonicalized.'}` — a dict with no `merged`, no `merged_at` and no `state` — and `str(pr.get('state') or 'open')` turned it into LIVE with a `why` reading `PR #None for 'b' is OPEN`. A definite answer the code never established, about a pull request it never saw. CHARACTERISED over the payload shapes: an ERROR body -> live; an EMPTY object -> live; a STRING -> undecidable; a LIST -> undecidable — so the collapse is specific to a DICT that answers nothing, which is exactly what a GitHub error body is. ⚠️ IT FAILED IN THE CAUTIOUS DIRECTION and nothing unsafe happened (LIVE sets safe_to_displace=False, so the worst outcome was a claimant declining to take a slot it could have had); filed MEDIUM for that reason and NOT as harmless, because the module's entire premise is that `we could not look` must never wear a definite answer and this is that failure one level in from the presence-is-not-liveness refusal it was built for. ⚠️ AND THE `why` WAS THE DANGEROUS PART, NOT THE STATE: a session reading `PR #None ... is OPEN` would reasonably conclude a live PR had been read and could go looking for one that does not exist — unprovenanced diagnostic output, sub-class A. THE FIX: a payload is authoritative only when it ANSWERS (`merged`/`merged_at`, or a `state` in {open, closed, merged}); anything else falls through to the branch-presence proxy AND SAYS SO, because falling through silently would leave a reader thinking no payload was supplied, which is a different fact pointing at a different fix. The proxy stays decisive where it is decisive — a branch GONE from origin still grades SPENT even on an unusable payload — and `PR #None` is replaced by `(no number in the payload)`. VERIFICATION: 11 new controls (35 in the file), 7 planted defects, 7 caught, positive control quiet on restore, including a POSITIVE control that open/closed/merged still decide, without which a change grading every payload `undecidable` would pass every other assertion and destroy the direct answer the module is built around; --self-test still passes and the 24 pre-existing cases are unmodified. ⚠️ WHAT THIS DOES NOT CLOSE: nothing has measured how many other callers in this repo default a missing API field to a plausible value, and the row says so rather than implying the sweep was done. ⚠️ AND A NOTED FOLLOW-ON NOT FIXED HERE: the slot's `purpose` is free text and this tool's only route to the direct answer is a PR number parsed out of it, so a claim whose purpose omits `#NNNN` forces the proxy — which is precisely the claim that produced this defect, written by this session.
